visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The scene opens in a brightly lit indoor conference room where a man in a brown uniform, acting as a boss, stands before a table. Three colleagues, one man and two women, are seated, listening intently. A large digital screen in the background displays a presentation title about a board meeting for 'Seriously Super Junior.' (2) A woman enters the frame pushing a black baby stroller, bringing it to the center of the room. The boss gestures toward the stroller with an open palm as the camera cuts to a medium close-up of a baby sitting inside, wearing a small bib and looking around with wide eyes. (3) A series of black-and-white edited images appear, showing the baby superimposed into various industrial and professional environments, such as a construction site with a power plant and an F1 racing pit. The lighting shifts to high contrast for these mock-professional montages. (4) The camera cuts back to the conference room where the seated man in the brown shirt expresses visible frustration, gesturing with his hands and leaning forward to object. The two women smile and point toward the baby, displaying supportive facial expressions. (5) In a different office setting with desks and computer monitors in the background, the man in the brown shirt leans over the stroller to talk to the baby. The baby responds with various facial movements like pouting and staring. (6) A woman sits in a grey office chair, looking directly into the camera and speaking while gesturing with her hands. The baby is shown crying loudly in a close-up shot with visible tears and a wide-open mouth. (7) The boss is seen sitting in a black executive chair, holding the baby on his lap. He holds a glass of white milk to the baby's mouth, and the baby drinks calmly while staring ahead.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a clear male voice speaking in a calm, professional narrative tone, welcoming people to a meeting. A subtle, low-energy background music track with a light electronic beat plays underneath the speech. (2) A sudden 'ding' sound effect triggers a transition as a female voice enters the mix, apologizing for being late with an upbeat and slightly breathless delivery. (3) The boss's voice returns, introducing the new 'Vice President' with higher vocal arousal. A burst of canned applause and cheering SFX is layered into the mix as the music tempo seems to increase slightly. (4) A percussive 'impact' sound effect occurs when the employee raises his objection. His voice is loud, characterized by sharp pitch variability and high intensity, expressing comedic frustration. (5) The baby's sounds, consisting of high-pitched gurgles and soft vocalizations, are introduced. These are followed by an intentional digital 'pop' sound effect asvariety subtitles appear visually. (6) A sharp cartoonish 'whoosh' sound effect accompanies the crying baby, which has a wide spectral bandwidth and high volume. A female voice provides a rhythmic, flat-toned 'translation' of the baby's cries. (7) The video concludes with an upbeat, high-energy pop track with a strong bass beat and prominent synthesizer chords as the boss holds the baby, accompanied by the faint sound of liquid sloshing in a glass.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a humorous skit to engage the audience through absurdity and cute visuals. By 'promoting' a baby to a high corporate position, the content satirizes traditional workplace hierarchies and seniority, ultimately serving to humanize the brand 'Seriously Super Junior' and drive engagement via social media trends.
